dharana.numbering_edition: Jaideva Singh 1979 (dhāraṇā 1 = verse 24; dhāraṇā 82 = verses 105–106 and dhāraṇā 89 = verses 113–114, otherwise one verse each; dhāraṇā 112 = verse 137)
dharana.sanskrit_iast: ghaṭādau yac ca vijñānam icchādyaṃ vā mamāntare | naiva sarvagataṃ jātam bhāvayann iti sarvagaḥ || grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittiḥ sāmānyā sarvadehinām | yogināṃ tu viśeṣo 'sti sambandhe sāvadhānatā ||
dharana.sanskrit_source: GRETIL e-text, compared with Wallis's concordance, Pradīpaka and the Singh scan
sanskrit_variants: verse 105: Sandhi corrected: GRETIL bhāvayan iti; Wallis bhāvayann iti.
verse 106: GRETIL encoding artefact '=B9' restored as avagraha: viśeṣo 'sti.
dharana.rendering: (105) 'The knowing, willing and the rest that are in me are not in me alone; they arise in everything, in a pot and other things too': contemplating this, one becomes all-pervading. (106) The awareness of object and subject is common to all embodied beings; the yogīs' distinction is that they stay attentive to the relation between them.
dharana.rendering_attribution: School paraphrase drawing on Jaideva Singh (1979), Christopher Wallis and Bettina Bäumer (as printed in Wallis's concordance); not a quotation.
dharana.commentary_note: Singh: knowing (jñāna) and willing/acting (icchā, kriyā) are not the monopoly of human beings but common to everything; contemplating this, one sheds insularity and feels kinship with all. He quotes Abhinavagupta and Somānanda: 'I know as one with the jar'. Singh states that verse 106 contains no separate dhāraṇā; it reinforces 105 by naming the yogī's distinction: mindfulness of the witnessing awareness to which every object is related. Wallis counts the two verses as separate yuktis: 'consciousness in everything' (Y80) and 'pay attention to the connection' (Y81).
dharana.technique_name: Knowing and Willing in Everything, and Attention to the Link
dharana.instruction: Recognise your own knowing and willing in everything around you, and stay aware of the link between knower and known.

checked_against: Jaideva Singh 1979 (scanned copy): '[Dhāraṇā 82] VERSE 105' followed by 'VERSE 106' with no dhāraṇā heading (Singh: verse 106 'only gives the special characteristic of a Yogi and re-inforces the idea contained in the previous dhāraṇā')
The Mystery Within (2019), Session Two list: 'Dharana 82' = verse 105–106 (agrees with Singh)
Wallis concordance: verse 105 = 'Consciousness in everything (Y80 ~ B3)'; verse 106 = 'Pay attention to the connection (Y81 ~ B3)' (verse text and technique match)
GRETIL, Wallis and Pradīpaka: Sanskrit of verse 105–106 compared
verification.notes: Door index = Singh dhāraṇā number, read directly in Singh's own headings and cross-checked against The Mystery Within's Singh-numbered list and Wallis's concordance. Caveat: Singh was read from an OCR scan, not a print copy in hand.

numbering_variants.wallis_yukti: verse 105: Consciousness in everything (Y80 ~ B3); verse 106: Pay attention to the connection (Y81 ~ B3)
numbering_variants.mystery_within_parallel: The parallel-translations section of The Mystery Within labels verse 105 'Dharana 82' (agrees) but verse 106 'Dharana 83'. Singh and the same book's Session Two count verse 106 as part of dhāraṇā 82, not a separate dhāraṇā. Not followed.
numbering_variants.two_verses: Singh heads verses 105 and 106 as one dhāraṇā (82) and notes that 106 contains no separate dhāraṇā; Wallis counts them as two yuktis (Y80, Y81).

source_disagreements: Grouping: Singh counts verse 106 as part of dhāraṇā 82 (no separate dhāraṇā); Wallis counts verse 106 as its own yukti (Y81, 'pay attention to the connection'). The Mystery Within's Session Two list also groups 105–106 as Dhāraṇā 82.

seat.label: Any steady, comfortable position (school addition)
seat.summary: Any steady, comfortable position: sitting on a chair, sitting on the floor with support under the hips, or lying on the back. Standing or walking slowly is also acceptable when that is easier. Choose the position in which the body needs the least effort.
seat.honesty: School addition. Verse 105–106 does not specify a body position. The seat is a convenience so the dharana can be practised; it is not part of the technique and makes no claim of tradition.

points: the same in a pot, a stone, everything
the link between knower and known
geometry.summary: Not a body shape. The map is the same spark of knowing in oneself and in every object, and the thread that links knower to known.
geometry.svg_hint: a figure and a simple pot, each with the same small spark, joined by a fine line
geometry.honesty: Geometry records the dharana's own map of attention, not a body shape. Locations marked 'commentarial' come from commentary, not from the verse.

reaction.name: Kinship with all
reaction.summary: School metaphor only: the sense that only 'I' knows and wants is replaced by kinship with everything, while attention rests on the link between knower and known. Not a biochemical or medical claim.

breath.lands_in: wherever the breath naturally ends; this door places nothing on the breath
breath.cue: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps you settle, then let the count go. No forced hold.
breath.honesty: The counts are an optional school pacing aid, not part of the verse. Hold is always 0: this school never adds a deliberate breath-hold.

orientation.cue: Turn attention toward what the verse names, and let everything else stay in the background
orientation.gravity: Let the floor or chair carry the body completely; there is no posture to hold
orientation.degrees_hint: No angle target: the VBT gives no posture for this dharana

attention.primary: Knowing and willing recognised as present in everything, not only in oneself
attention.secondary: The relation between the one who knows and what is known

adiyogi.verse_paraphrase: (105) 'The knowing, willing and the rest that are in me are not in me alone; they arise in everything, in a pot and other things too': contemplating this, one becomes all-pervading. (106) The awareness of object and subject is common to all embodied beings; the yogīs' distinction is that they stay attentive to the relation between them.
adiyogi.method_summary: Contemplate that the knowing and willing you feel in yourself are present in everything around you: a pot, a stone, a cloud. Then, as you look at any object, stay attentive to the link between you, the knower, and it, the known.

honesty.disclosure: Door 082 follows Vijñāna Bhairava Tantra dharana 82 (verse 105–106) in Jaideva Singh's numbering. The door-to-dharana index is a School of 112 Doorways teaching device. Singh's sequence is one edition's count, not an ancient one-to-one canon. The seat, counts, reaction and beat scripts are school additions.
honesty.notes: pairing_type is school_device: the dharana is the content, while the door index, seat and pacing are the school's.

safety.pain_rule: Pain is information. Pause, regress, or exit. Never push through sharp pain.
safety.open_seat_alternate: This door needs no particular posture: sit on a chair, sit on the floor with support, or lie down. Eyes may stay open.
safety.contraindication_notes: General practice caution only; not medical advice. A contemplation, not a belief to be forced; let it remain light. If anything feels distressing (dizziness, agitation, strong emotion), stop, open the eyes and rest attention on the feet and the floor.

beats.title: Geometry
beats.script: No shape to make. Sit with the eyes open or closed. The map is the same spark in you and in every object.

beats.title: Orientation
beats.script: Let the floor or the chair carry you. Eyes closed or soft.

beats.title: Breath
beats.script: Natural breath. Count about four in and four out only if it helps. No forced hold.

beats.title: Attention
beats.script: Feel your own knowing and willing. See the same in the pot, the stone, the cloud. Then stay aware of the link between you and what you see.

beats.title: Reaction cue
beats.script: School image: one spark in every object. A metaphor, not medicine.

beats.title: Adiyogi thread
beats.script: Verse 105–106: the knowing and willing in me are in all things, even a pot; contemplating so, one becomes all-pervading. The yogī stays attentive to the link between knower and known.

beats.title: Exit / integrate
beats.script: Let the breath go unwatched for a round. Move the fingers and toes. Return to the room.
